Notes.Text:
This update for scribus fixes the following issues:

Changes in scribus:

- Update to 1.6.7
  * Fixes CVE-2026-104061 / boo#1289047
  * Fixes CVE-2026-104062 / boo#1289046
  * Fixes CVE-2026-104063 / boo#1289045
  * Fixes CVE-2026-104064 / boo#1289044
  * Fixes CVE-2026-104065 / boo#1289043
  * Fixes CVE-2026-104066 / boo#1289042
  * Fixes CVE-2026-104067 / boo#1289041
  * [Text Frames / Story Editor] Superscript text: the text
    outline is offset
  * [Import / Export] Property changes do not affect the text
    imported from .odt
  * [Canvas] Rendering of drop shadows is slow (Fahad)
  * [General] The application freezes when attempting to import
    'custom shapes'
  * [Undo/Redo] Deleting a non existent mark causes crash
  * [General] Preview mode does not hide guides/margins when
    editing a master page
  * [General] The bleed area still shows in Preview mode in
    Master Page editing mode
  * [Typography] Text formatting (e.g. italic, bold) is not
    inherited when resuming typing
  * [General] Failure to build with poppler 26.07.0
  * [Graphics / Image Frames] Crash with graphicsmagick exception
  * [General] Failure to build with poppler 26.06.0
  * [General] Failure to build with poppler 26.05.0
  * [Fonts] Font "Helsinki" causes crash

- Fix failure to build with poppler 26.05.0 (boo#1265939)
- Change scribus-doc sub-package to noarch.

- Update to 1.6.6
  * [Scripter] Add get/setImageRotation to Scripter
  * [Graphics / Image Frames] Lost image links after collect for
    output
  * [General] Failure to build with poppler 26.04.0
  * [General] Failure to build with poppler 26.03.0
  * [Import / Export] MS Publisher import needs more
    development: Image scaling
  * [Plug-ins] Fix bad escape sequences in Python docstring
  * [General] Failure to build with poppler 26.02.0
  * [Plug-ins] Color wheel doesn't move to correct color
  * [PDF] Scribus crashes due to umlaut composition in file names
    of embedded PDF documents

- Update to 1.6.5
  * [General]  NTLM hash leak in Scribus
  * [User Interface]  Dark Color Schema unusable
  * [Color Management]  Color picker (eyedropper) does not work
    (always returns "black")
  * [General]  Layer disappears after editing inline object
    (layer visibility scrambling)
  * [General]  Failure to build with poppler 25.10.0
  * [PDF]  Scribus crashes when exporting pdf via python and the
    document has a PDF-Push-Button or other PDF-thingy
  * [Build System]  Won't Compile: 'const_key_value_iterator' does
    not name a type
  * [Styles]  The line spacing mode drop down is not correctly
    displayed for styles with a parent
  * [Build System]  Fails to build with poppler 25.07
  * [PDF]  Build failure with podofo 1.0
  * [Scripter]  Undocumented feature in scribus.ImageExport: transparentBckgnd
  * [Scripter]  Documentation of function getBoundingBox()
    missing from HTML docs
  * [Fonts]  Additional Font Path Settings reset
  * [General]  Crash when loading legacy file produced with
    Scribus 1.4.6
  * [Scripter]  Using unknown/misspelled named parameter in API
    call causes Scribus crash
  * [Canvas]  Sometimes all items in a document become invisible
  * [General]  Failure to build with poppler 25.09.0
  * [General]  Accept negative values for the rotation in the
    properties palette
  * [General]  1.6.4 fails to build with popper 25.06.0
  * [Fonts]  Font rendering different after PDF export
  * [Printing]  Print Dialog - Inconsistency between output
    filename extension and printing language
  * [Printing]  Print Dialog - Crop marks not present in output
    when they are the only marks selected

Vulnerabilities.Description: Scribus before 1.6.7 and 1.7.x before 1.7.4 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the scimgdataloader_psd loader that uses unchecked PSD file values as lookup array indexes. Attackers can convince users to place or import a crafted PSD file to corrupt heap memory, causing crashes and potentially code execution as the user.

Scribus before 1.6.7 and 1.7.x before 1.7.4 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in the PICT image loader and import plugin that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory by supplying an unchecked bytesPerLine value. Attackers can craft a PICT file whose bytesPerLine exceeds the QImage scanline size, so placing or importing it crashes Scribus and may execute code as the user.

Scribus before 1.6.7 and 1.7.x before 1.7.4 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the Mac PICT image loader and import plugin when decoding planar pixel data. Attackers can supply a crafted PICT file with manipulated dimensions that, when placed or imported, causes heap over-reads leading to crashes or heap memory disclosure.

Scribus before 1.6.7 and 1.7.x before 1.7.4 contains an integer overflow vulnerability in the scimgdataloader_tiff TIFF loader that allows attackers to trigger a heap overflow via crafted tile dimensions. Attackers can supply a tiled TIFF with large tile width, height and sample values for a user to import, corrupting heap memory to crash Scribus or execute code.

Scribus before 1.6.7 and 1.7.x before 1.7.4 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the importdrw Micrografx Draw plugin that uses an unvalidated y offset to select image scanlines. Attackers can craft a DRW file that, when imported by a user, writes decoded bitmap data outside the heap image buffer, causing crashes or code execution.

Scribus before 1.6.7 and 1.7.x before 1.7.4 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in the Mac PICT image loader and import plugin when unpacking 4-bit indexed pixel data. Attackers can supply a crafted PICT file with inconsistent width and row data that, when placed or imported, writes out of bounds, causing crashes or code execution.

Scribus before 1.6.7 and 1.7.x before 1.7.4 contains an out-of-bounds memory access vulnerability in the importsvm plugin that fails to verify bitmap and transparency mask dimensions match. Attackers can supply a crafted SVM file with mismatched mask dimensions to trigger heap reads and writes, causing crashes or code execution as the user.
